scenarioName: Pneumonia — Mild Hypoxia, Supportive BLS Care

scenarioStory.history: Daughter reports patient has had a productive cough with yellow-green sputum, subjective fevers, and chills for two days, now with increasing fatigue and mild shortness of breath, worse with exertion. No chest pain. No known sick contacts. Patient lives alone and daughter checked in after she didn't answer the phone this morning.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 74-year-old female seated upright in a recliner, tired-appearing, with a frequent productive cough and mild increased work of breathing. → Oxygen and positioning provided: Crew applies supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula titrated to target saturation, keeps the patient in a position of comfort, and continues monitoring while preparing for transport. → Reassessed and prepared for transport: Patient's oxygenation and comfort have improved with supplemental oxygen and positioning; crew continues serial reassessment and supportive care en route.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Productive cough, fever, and feeling weak and short of breath for two days

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 74-year-old female seated upright in a recliner, tired-appearing, with a frequent productive cough and mild increased work of breathing.

scenarioEvents.name: Oxygen and positioning provided
scenarioEvents.description: Crew applies supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula titrated to target saturation, keeps the patient in a position of comfort, and continues monitoring while preparing for transport.
relatedChecklist: Assess full vital signs, breath sounds, and mental status
Apply nasal cannula O2 titrated to 94–98% SpO2
Position patient upright in position of comfort

scenarioEvents.name: Reassessed and prepared for transport
scenarioEvents.description: Patient's oxygenation and comfort have improved with supplemental oxygen and positioning; crew continues serial reassessment and supportive care en route.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs and response to oxygen/positioning en route

scenarioEvents.name: Oxygen delayed
scenarioEvents.description: Without prompt supplemental oxygen, the patient's hypoxia and work of breathing worsen, with increasing accessory muscle use and anxiety.
relatedChecklist: Recognize worsening hypoxia; apply O2 titrated to 94–98% SpO2 without further delay
